messages:
Priya (Finance): Heads-up: Acme reached out about their March invoice. Their internal telemetry shows ~12.1K embed attempts in a short burst but our invoice billed ~7.3K. They see a lot of 429s on their side and want an explanation.

Maya (Finance Manager): Do we bill on attempts or only on successful ledger writes? If it's the latter, we need to explain and decide if a goodwill credit is appropriate.

Alex (Eng-Ingest): Short answer: we bill successful ingests only. Our ingest pipeline writes to embed_ledger when the request is accepted; transient retries that never make it to the ledger are not counted.

Sam (SRE): Can you provide example request ids/time window so I can look for rate-limiter drops?

Priya (Finance): Sent offline: window 2026-03-02 03:14-03:22 UTC, request_id prefix acme-7f2. Customer reports 12,100 raw attempts; invoice shows 7,321 embeds billed.

Alex (Eng-Ingest): Ran ledger query and rate-limiter logs. Ledger count for that prefix in window = 7321. Rate-limiter recorded ~4,800 drop events for the same prefix. So attempts ~= 12,121.

Jae (Platform): Clarifying: we have duplicate suppression and early-drop protections at the edge/load-balancer which can prevent retry floods from reaching ingest. Those drops are by design to protect downstream systems.

Priya (Finance): Understood. Customer expectations differ though; they think every produced embedding should be billable. Need policy/decision.

Maya (Finance Manager): Policy currently: billable units = successful ledger writes. But given this is a UX gap and caused by our protection, recommend a one-off goodwill credit and action items: (1) export attempts vs counted metric to billing UI; (2) add an alert for high drop ratio; (3) clearly document billing semantics. Approving credit up to $5k pending exact delta.

Alex (Eng-Ingest): I can prepare a backfill that inserts stub rows referencing the dropped attempts with meter_reason='retry_backfill' and a note. Backfill job id: backfill-20260302-acme-01. It would insert 4800 raw embeds -> translates to embed_units = ceil(4800/1000) = 5 units.

Priya (Finance): Need to compute dollar impact. What is per-embed-unit price?

Alex (Eng-Ingest): Our ledger stores embed_units (1000-embed unit). If unit price = $384 (as in this account's contract), 5 * $384 = $1,920. That matches the customer's reported delta.

Maya (Finance Manager): Approve one-time credit of $1,920. Priya draft communications. Also create a P2 ticket for Platform to publish attempts vs counted metric and a P3 for docs update.

Priya (Finance): Will draft email with backfill job id and numbers. Alex please paste SQL preview and run in staging so I can verify numbers before issuing credit.

Alex (Eng-Ingest): SQL preview for staging backfill: ```sql
INSERT INTO embed_ledger (customer_id, created_at, request_id, embeds_count, embed_units, meter_reason, note)
VALUES ('acme','2026-03-02T03:18:00Z','acme-7f2-backfill-1',4800,5,'retry_backfill','goodwill credit; backfill-20260302-acme-01');
```

billing-bot: Backfill job backfill-20260302-acme-01 created in staging. Estimated invoice delta: $1,920. Tagging @billing.

Sam (SRE): Recommend adding alert: if any customer has (rate_limiter.dropped / attempts) > 0.2 over 5m window then page eng-infra and account owner. Also add a dashboard tile showing attempts vs counted per-customer for last 24h.

Jae (Platform): Agree. Long-term we can offer an opt-in flag for customers who prefer attempts to be treated as billable truth, but that requires anti-fraud and rate limits on backfilled billing. For now telemetry + one-off credit is fine.

Maya (Finance Manager): Thanks. Actions: Priya send credit email, create Platform ticket for attempts vs counted (P2), file postmortem note (blameless) and record credit. Alex run the staging backfill and confirm results. Closing thread after comms sent. :white_check_mark:
